plan: This is a second-price auction where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the weakly dominant strategy - it maximizes expected profit regardless of what others bid. Bidding above value risks paying more than the item is worth to me if I win against a bid between my value and my bid. Bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my private value of $31.

This is a second-price auction (winner pays second-highest bid), where bidding your true value is the dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I never overpay (since I'd only pay what others bid, which would be less than my value if I win) and never miss out on profitable wins. Bidding higher risks overpaying if I win at a price above my value; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $22, I will bid exactly $22 to maximize expected profit.

This is a second-price auction where bidding my true value is the dominant strategy. Since I pay the second-highest bid if I win (not my own bid), there's no incentive to shade my bid up or down. Bidding exactly my value of $40 ensures I win whenever the item is worth more to me than the price I'd pay, and I never overpay since the price is determined by the second-highest bid. This maximizes my expected profit given the auction mechanics.
